newsitem.title: CANADA: Northern Telecom posts improved Q4 profits.
newsitem.headline: Northern Telecom posts improved Q4 profits.

text.p: Canadian telecommunications equipment firm Northern Telecom Ltd. posted stronger fourth-quarter and full-year earnings on Monday and executives were upbeat about prospects for 1997.
Nortel's sales rose 20 percent to $4.19 billion in the fourth quarter from $3.50 billion in the year-earlier period. Net earnings per share rose to $1.23 from 98 cents in the fourth quarter of 1995.
Order input for the fourth quarter was a record $5.27 billion, a 41 percent increase from the $3.74 billion in the same quarter of previous year.
For the full year, the company posted sales of $12.85 billion, 20 percent above the $10.67 billion in 1995. Net earnings advanced to $2.40 a share from $1.85 a share.
Nortel Chief Executive Jean Monty told Reuters in a telephone interview he was pleased with the company's 1996 performance and felt confident about prospects in 1997.
"Revenues have grown at 20 percent -- we're a sizeable company to be able to have a growth rate at that level. And earnings continue to grow faster than revenues," Monty said.
UBS Securities analyst Nikos Theodosopoulos said bookings, profits and gross margins were ahead of analysts' expectations, with only switching revenues and administrative costs disappointing.
Monty said 1997 sales would top the 12-14 percent minimum growth target range the company had given to analysts.

"We will grow by more than 12 to 14 percent, which is the range of minimum growth that we had put out to the analysts," Monty said. "And the bottom line will grow by more than the top line. Margins will improve."
Nortel stock was off C$1.60 to C$92 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday. In New York, Nortel was 75 cents lower at $68.625.
